rationale: ChatGPT previously accepted both generic stems because each choice is a complete proposition and each record has exactly one defensible answer.
The zero case is self-opposite, so it tests a boundary case rather than a number substitution.
Absolute value at zero is a boundary case distinct from the distance of a nonzero value.
The records test unlike signs, additive inverses, and exponent precedence; normalization erased the decisive operators.
The second record uses zero minus a negative number, a sign boundary case rather than a value-only substitution.
Exponent one and exponent zero require different exponent laws and yield different conceptual conclusions.
Large and sub-unit decimals require opposite decimal-point directions and positive versus negative powers of ten.
